Resources.Name: Particle board
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative for a standard construction chipboard without special treatment or additive materials. If such a variant of the board is used, an EPD can be used if possible or this data can be used as a proxy.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Standard particle board is typically used as surface material in a protected environment, typically indoors.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for standard chip board typically varies between 0.35-0.45 kg CO₂e/kg based on Nordic and Middle-European EPDs. The average data values are based on EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Norway and Finland.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Chipboards are made of wood chips and resin pressed together. The amount of glue is about 10 %. By-products from the manufaturing of sawn timber are utilised in the production of chipboards. Densities vary between 650 and 750 kg/m³.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process  and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: A particle board can have different treatment, coating, etc. that is applicable to different applications that are not considered here but apply to a standard product.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, but significant import occurs from (given in relative order): Norway, Finland and Europe.

Resources.Name: Glasswool, batts and rolls
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative for the product type glasswool as batts or rolls and includes all types of thermal insulation that do not include any surfacing. In the case that surfacing is included, a more precise and exact choice should be made; such products typically have higher climate impact per kg.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Glasswool is used as thermal insulation and sometimes also used as sound insulation or as a combined function. Glass wool is intended to be used in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for non-coated glasswool, batts and rolls. The GWP may vary between 0.7-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg based on the manufacturer. The average data values are based on EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Germany and Poland.
Resources.Synonyms: Glass wool, mineral glass wool, mineral wool, batts, boards, panels, thermal insulation
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Glass wool is produced in an electric furnace. The process involves primary raw materials and energy sources, both of which contribute to the GWP. The proportion of recycled glass used as raw material varies between 40 and 80%. The amount of binder is approximately 5 to 10%. There is a minor variation in density for the same lambda value between different manufacturers, but the density values given here, as well as the lambda value, are representative of the products used on the Swedish market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal to the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: To assess thermal insulation, the lambda value must be used in combination with the fact that different product options have different densities. In other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kilogram, but rather within a given building application. The material data for the generic resource is as follows: density 18.7 kg/m³ and lambda value 0.035 W/(mK).
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, but significant import occurs from (given in relative order): Germany, Poland and Europe.

Resources.Name: Sawn timber, u 16 %, coniferous
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative of sawn dried timber and can be used as it is, but is mainly used as a raw material in planed wood production.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Sawn timber can be used directly as it is and serves as a raw material for impregnated wood. When it is planed, it is used for other wood-based products. Sawn timber is used in construction for formwork and structural timber, for so-called cladding timber for panels, as well as planed for flooring or joinery timber for windows, doors, and interior fittings, etc. The wood is usually refined by planing, profiling, gluing, finger-jointing, or impregnation depending on the area of use.
Resources.GeneralComment: Input are collected from 44 sawmills and cover the production of 10 190 000 m³ sawn dried timber. Data to produce sawn wood is collected from a representative selection of sawmills in Sweden and weighted to an average. Sawn dried timber that is produced in Sweden is mainly based on domestic logs. The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for sawn timbers varies between 21-37 kg CO₂e/m³ for the companies that are involved (and based on the methodology and inventory data used).
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The climate impact is based on a sector EPD that cover 58 % of the total sawn softwood timber in Sweden. Dried sawn timber has an average density of 455 kg/m³ and moisture content of 16 %. Sawn dried timber of spruce has an average density of 470 kg/m³ and 440 kg/m³ for pine. The moisture content for the dried wood is about 12-18 %. Biogenic carbon storage is 715kg CO₂/m³.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the major producers and thereby the major consumption of sawn timber used in Sweden. These data represent the year 2020, i.e. after reduction diesel was implemented why the GWP reported is lower than before.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of wood indoors is normally equal to the construction of which it is part of. Wood exposed to outdoors normally needs maintenance during these 50 years lifespan.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When the products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers, which is why the background data used from Swedish sawmills can be considered representative of this consumption.

Resources.Name: Electricity, Swedish mix
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data represents Swedish electricity mix, including exports and imports.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Electricity is purchased from the electricity grid for several purposes.
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG is an average value from 2015 to 2017 and is based on annual statistics published by Entso-E. The electricity climate impact has been calculated using the methodology defined in the Fuel Quality Directive 98/70/EC and with regard to clarification in a supplementary directive (EC) 2015/652, which deals with the determination of calculation methods and reporting requirements for fuels, and the Renewable Energy Directive (EU) 2018/2001. The calculations thus follow both EN 15804 and in the way the Swedish Energy Agency considers that the environmental impact from electricity production and use of various fuels and energy carriers must be reported. See IVL report No. C433 for more information.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The calculations are performed in the LCA tool Gabi and upstream LCA data for electricity based on processes representative of the facilities in Sweden. The environmental impact is calculated as annual production and imports/exports, which means that emissions differ between the years, which is why it is common to recommend a floating three-year average for this type of process.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: Data is representative for the years 2015 to 2017.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: Different inventory methods are used, which is why other LCA data may not be comparable to the method used here.

Resources.Name: Diesel MK1, reduction obligation (2024)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Environmental data is representative of the diesel purchased in Sweden. Diesel's climate performance is governed by the reduction obligation and increased amount of biofuels, which is determined by the government. The Swedish Energy Agency has produced a new regulation, STEMFS 2025:​3, on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions through the incorporation of biofuels in petrol and diesel fuels.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Diesel is purchased and burned in various machines and vehicles, i.e. a WtW (Well to Wheel) scope.
Resources.GeneralComment: The climate impact from Diesel MK1 was 89,9 g CO₂e/MJ, the share of renewable energy was 6,3 percent in 2024 (Energimyndigheten Drivmedel 2024).
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The calculation of greenhouse gas emissions according to the reduction obligation is based on the standard values ​​for the fossil fuels established in an additional directive to the fuel quality directive 2015/652/EU and a mixture of renewables.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: Data is representative for the year 2024.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The calculation method follows "Renewable Energy Directive" (RED) 2018/2001/EU and the “FQD Implementing Directive” EU 2015/652. However, there is a difference between these directives compared to core product calculations rules for construction products (EN 15804). The major difference is that EN 15804 use an economical allocation approach for pre-consumer waste/recycling, why fuels based on this kind of raw materials would result in a higher value if EN 15804 was to be followed. This difference is not relevant for the LCA figures given here, but may arise if these data are replaced with specific LCA data from a manufacturer that complies with the EC directives.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The data is representative for diesel purchased in Sweden.

Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
The calculation of greenhouse gas emissions according to the reduction obligation is based on the standard values for fossil fuels established in an additional directive to the “FQD Implementing Directive” 2015/652/EU and the blend of biodiesel. These values are:
• Petrol 93.3 g CO₂e/MJ
• Diesel 95.1 g CO₂e/MJ
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: Data is representative for the year 2024.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The calculation method follows "Renewable Energy Directive" (RED) 2018/2001/EU and the “FQD Implementing Directive” EU 2015/652. This difference is not relevant for the LCA values stated here, but may arise if this information is replaced by specific LCA data from a manufacturer that complies with the EC directive.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The data is representative for 100% fossil diesel. If other diesel is used, other data shall be used.

Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is supplied by import mainly from Germany.

Resources.Name: Plywood (spruce or pine)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of a plywood consisting of thin wood veneers that are cross-laminated, glued, heat-treated, and pressed under high pressure. This results in a dimensionally stable and strong board.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Plywood is commonly used as a surface material in a protected environment from weather exposure or indoors. Plywood is available as unclassified building plywood and as classified structural plywood. Structural plywood is used, for example, behind plasterboards in standard stud walls to allow heavier items to be screwed onto the finished wall. Structural plywood is manufactured in two different classes: 15/50 and 20/70 (bending strength in MPa/modulus of elasticity in MPa).
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP (A1-A3) for wood-based panels can vary greatly between different manufacturers. To achieve a comment result, the biogenic carbon stored in products is subtracted, so that the climate impact is reported as GWP-GHG. Even after this, there can be significant differences between manufacturers which, without access to the underlying LCA report, are difficult to explain. One difference may be the environmental impact allocated to the wood raw material. For plywood, climate impact has thus been corrected for a producer (i.e. reduced). The difference after correction is less than 10 % between producers.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Data is valid for plywood made of spruce or pine and about 10 % resin . Densities between different producers varies +/-5 %.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing processes and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The specific board is designed to be used indoors and has a common thickness of 12 mm.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is partly covered by national production, but significant imports come mainly from Finland and other nearby countries.

Resources.Name: OSB
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: OSB (Oriented Strand Board) can be described in terms of its structure as something between chipboard and plywood. However, its technical properties are most comparable to plywood. The boards are manufactured by gluing together long, flat wood strands under pressure and heat.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: OSB is commonly used as a surface material in a protected environment from weather exposure or indoors.
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP (A1-A3) for wood-based panels can vary greatly between different manufacturers. To achieve a comment result, the biogenic carbon stored in products is subtracted, so that the climate impact is reported as GWP-GHG. One difference may be the environmental impact allocated to the wood raw material.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The data refers to OSB made from conifer with resin content of less than 10%. The density may vary by up to ±5% between different manufacturers.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that are currently consumed on the market. Data are valid until new ones are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of the product is normally equal to the service life of the construction of which it is a part.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The specific board is designed to be used indoors and a common thickness is 11 or 15 mm.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption of boards in Sweden is based on import.

Resources.Name: Ready-mix made concrete, buildings C20/25
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet:
The compressive strength classes refer to concrete used for buildings with a concrete composition and binder mix representative of the Swedish market. If more properties are required for a concrete, information from a supplier must be used. Normally, concrete is reinforced. Reinforcement is handled as a separate resource in this database.
For testing compressive strength, EN 206 refers to the following standard: EN 12390-3, Testing hardened concrete — Part 3: Compressive strength of test specimens. In Table 12 of EN 206 specifies "Compressive strength classes for normal concrete and heavy concrete". This is supplemented in SS 137003 with "Table 1 — Intermediate classes for compressive strength".
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Concrete for houses is used especially for load-bearing parts of the structure. The concrete composition is controlled, in addition to compressive strength of exposure class, but also of other properties e.g. consistence, time for curing and drying.
Resources.GeneralComment: Concrete is made from rock, gravel and cement where the main raw material is limestone. In climate-improved concrete is part of the cement replaced with alternative binders. The data given, based on compressive strength class, represent commonly used concrete recipes on the market. Factory data for module A3 is based on data from a large number of EPDs. Of the reported value for climate impact, the contribution from the manufacturing process (A3) is relatively small in relation to the contribution from the cement, which normally accounts for more than 90 % of the concrete's climate impact in module A1-A3. Environmental data for the cement binders used are based on EPDs for commonly used cement grades on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The compressive strength class of the concrete follows the standard EN 206:2013+A1:2016 and SS 137003:2015.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The provided data are representative of the Swedish producers of ready-mixed concrete and the concrete recipes they use. This information was collected in 2020. The environmental impact data are based on current EPDs for binders as well as factory data.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: Concrete exposed to outdoors or other wet environment is designed in respect to durability according to Eurocodes. The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Concrete for buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When concrete products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, i.e. the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Concrete manufacturers are spread across the entire country, and the environmental data can be considered representative since the concrete recipes used, as well as the binder mix, reflect the production of all these manufacturers and are also based on several EPDs.

Resources.Name: Clay roof tiles
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for clay roof tiles used on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Clay tiles are normally without glaze and the most common shapes are 1-barrel, the 2-barrel and flat tiles. Clay tiles require a pitched roof and waterproof underlayment.
Resources.GeneralComment: Clay tiles are manufactured of clay, sand and lime. The bricks are burned in a tunnel furnace at a high temperature, roughly 1050 degrees. The primary energy use varies between 2.0 – 2,4 MJ/kg of nonrenewable energy and 0.5 MJ/kg of electricity. The use of combustion of fossil fuels is the dominant contribution to the products GHG emissions. Environmental data are based on an LCA study (Erlandsson and Jönsson 1992) that is updated in 2020 LCA valid for the domestic producer in Swedish. This figure has been verified with other EPDs, and EPDs based on bricks.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology used by the manufacturers is similar, but the fuel varies, with natural gas and oil being predominant. An addition of limestone powder to the clay produces yellow bricks. For brown or brown-black bricks, manganese is used. Roof tiles are fired in cassettes at 1050°C. The firing process itself takes two days in a modern tunnel kiln. The entire process is monitored to ensure that all roof tiles achieve uniform hardness and are frost-resistant.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the clay roof tiles that are consumed on the Swedish market. These data have been calulayted during the year 2020.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: Roofs with tiles are normally limited by the underlying waterproofing condition and its service life, where today you can assume a service life of up to 40 years for the underlayment and that clay roof tiles least 50 years. Resources.Name: Bricks, frost-resistant, hardburned
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of bricks used on the Swedish market where frost-resistant bricks are required, such as for chimneys, fireplaces, and other exposed surfaces where higher strength is needed.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability:
Hard-fired bricks are manufactured in various colors and sizes by different producers, but the common standard size is 228x108x54 mm (Danish standard). Previously, large bricks (300x150x75 mm) or the Swedish standard (250x120x65 mm) were also available, but these are no longer produced. The hard-fired brick is somewhat darker in color and should be used for external chimney masonry. It is mainly used for chimneys, fireplaces, paving bricks, and other exposed surfaces where higher strength is required.
Hard-fired bricks do not absorb moisture in the same way, which improves frost resistance compared to regular bricks, making them suitable for paving or chimneys. Hard-fired material results in a brick with water absorption typically below 6% of its own weight. According to the Swedish National Board of Housing, Building and Planning’s building regulations, frost-resistant bricks must be used in chimneys above the roof, where exposure to the climate subjects the bricks to ice formation.
Resources.GeneralComment: Bricks are manufactured of clay, sand, lime and sawdust. The bricks are burned in a tunnel furnace at a high temperature, roughly 1050 degrees. The primary energy use varies between 2.0 – 4 MJ/kg of nonrenewable energy and 0.5 MJ/kg of electricity. The use of combustion of fossil fuels is the dominant contribution to the products GHG emissions. Environmental data are based EPD for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market, with a variation from 2.2 to 3.3 kg CO₂e/kg.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology used by the manufacturers is similar, but the fuel varies where fossil gas and oil dominate. An additive in the clay of limestone flour gives yellow brick. Manganese is used for brown or tan-black brick. Bricks are fired in cassettes at 1050 °C. The actual firing takes two days in a modern tunnel kiln. The whole process is monitored so that all roof tiles to achieve an even hardness and a frost-resistant tile. Bricks are tested for frost durability in accordance with BS EN 771-1:2011+A1:2015 and the highest performance in testing is “F2”.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the bricks that are consumed on the Swedish market. Environmental data is based on the producers EPD collected during 2020.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.  Bricks in buildings usually do not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life. Bricks are suitable for reuse.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When bricks are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: All bricks used in Sweden are imported (the last brickworks was located in Haga, Enköping and closed in 2020). The largest imports come from Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany.

Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for sand lime bricks used on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Calcium silicate sand lime bricks are used for masonry. Sand lime bricks can be used for load bearing structures or for decorative and functional purpose when used exterior or interior. Sand lime bricks is used indoor in interior walls, but is not so common in Sweden.
Resources.GeneralComment: The environmental impact for manufacturing dominates by the amount of Lime content in the calcium silicate bricks that varies from 8 to 12 %. Since the content of sand is high, about 88 – 92 %, it means the properties of these bricks depends on the characteristics of sand used. Environmental data are based EPD for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market, with a variation from 1.1 to 1.4 kg CO₂e/kg.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology used by the manufacturers is similar. The brick raw material mixture is molded into bricks using rotary table press which uses mechanical pressure to press the bricks. In the final stage, bricks are placed in autoclave where saturated steam pressure is released and the temperature inside the chamber is raised and the reaction process begins. Silica content in sand and calcium content in lime reacts and forms crystal like compound called calcium hypo silicate. This process is done for 6 to 12 hours.

Resources.GeneralComment: The environmental impact for manufacturing dominates by the clinker production and the amount of cement content in the lightweight aggregate block. Resources.Synonyms: Lightweight aggregate block, lightweight concrete block, lightweight expanded clay aggregate block, expanded clay block

Resources.Name: Floatglass (FG)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative of a non-treated window glass.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Float glass is used as a raw material for window manufacturing or insulating glass units and is typically not handled on the construction site. Flat glass (FG) refers to both coated and uncoated float glass. Float glass is a clear soda-lime silicate glass with parallel, fire-polished surfaces, and in some cases, metal oxide-based coatings are applied to modify the glass’s radiation properties (thermal insulation and/or solar control).
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for floatglass varies between 0.95-1.2 kg CO₂e/kg depending on the supplier. The LCA values ​​are based on the largest importers to Sweden and their EPDs.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The differences in the manufacturing processes and the composition of float glass are minor between manufacturers. All float glass are imported to Sweden, primarily from European countries, and are produced according to European standards.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the type of floatglass that is used in the Swedish market. The information is valid until new data are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is basically infinite, but in practice it corresponds to the time until the glazed building element, in which the glass is included, is demolished, which in this case is set to 50 years.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: Float glass is available in various thicknesses (4 mm is common) and can be surface treated. However, these variations have no significant impact on GWP-GHG (A1-A3) per kilogram.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden consists primarily of imports, mainly from Europe.

Resources.Name: Stone wool, batts and rolls
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data is representative of the stone wool product type in the form of batts and rolls, and includes all types of thermal insulation that do not have any surfacing, coatings, or similar treatments. If surfacing is included, a more precise and specific dataset should be selected, as such products typically have a somewhat higher environmental impact per kilogram.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Stone wool is primarily used as thermal insulation, and is sometimes also used for sound insulation or for a combination of both functions. This type of stone wool product is intended for use in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for non-coated stone wool, batts and rolls. The GWP may variy between 0.6-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg based on the manufacturer. The average data values are based on market share and EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Finland and Norway.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Stone wool is produced either in an electric furnace or, more commonly, in a cupola furnace. The process also involves the use of additional energy sources which, together with the primary raw materials, contribute to the GWP. The binder content is typically about 5 to 10%. Minor variations in density for the same lambda value exist between different manufacturers, but the density and lambda values provided here are representative of the products used on the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative of the manufacturing process  and products that is currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: In order to assess thermal insulation, the lambda value needs to be used in combination with the fact that different product alternatives have different densities. In other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kg, but instead in use conditions. Material data applicable for the generic resource are as follows; density 29 kg/m³ and lambda 0.036 W/(mK).
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by Nordic producers and Germany (in the following order): Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Finland and Norway.

Resources.Name: Stone wool, plasterboard
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data is representative of the stone wool product type in the form of batts or rolls, and includes all types of thermal insulation that do not have any surfacing, coatings, or similar treatments. If surfacing is included, a more precise and specific dataset should be selected, as such products typically have a somewhat higher environmental impact per kilogram.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Stone wool is primarily used as thermal insulation, and is sometimes also used for sound insulation or for a combination of both functions. This type of stone wool product is intended for use in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) are valid for non-coated stone wool, batts and rolls. The GWP may vary between 0.6-1.6 kg CO₂e/kg. The average data values are based on market share and EPDs from the following countries (in order of assumed market share): Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Finland and Norway.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Stone wool is produced either in an electric furnace or, more commonly, in a cupola furnace. The process also involves the use of additional energy sources which, together with the primary raw materials, contribute to the GWP. The binder content is typically about 5 to 10%. Minor variations in density for the same lambda value exist between different manufacturers, but the density and lambda values provided here are representative of the products used on the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative of the manufacturing process  and products that is currently consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: In order to assess thermal insulation, the lambda value needs to be used in combination with the fact that different product alternatives have different densities. In other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kg, but instead in use conditions. Material data applicable for the generic resource are as follows; density 70 kg/m³ and lambda 0.033 W/(mK).
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by Nordic producers and Germany (in the following order): Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Finland and Norway.

Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of phenolic-based thermal insulation boards.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Phenolic insulation is used as thermal phenolic insulation for indoor and outdoor use.
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG (A1-A3) differs only marginally between different manufacturers. The majority of greenhouse gas emissions originate from the production of raw materials used in EPS manufacturing. The average data values are based on EPDs.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Rigid phenolic insulation is produced by mixing high solids and phenolic resin with a surface acting agent. The heat created by the reaction evaporates a volatile liquid blowing agent in the mixture which produces a network of small bubbles in the material. The foam can be cured to create one of two forms of the product. It can be manufactured by a continuous process to create thin sheet material which is laminated with various facings and cut into boards. Alternatively, it can be made into blocks to be cut into pre-determined shapes.

Resources.Name: Bitumen waterproofing membrane, top layer
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Polymer bitumen-based waterproofing layers are bitumen mats with reinforcement and cover mass of polymer bitumen on both sides. A distinction is made between two types of polymer bitumen: elastomer bitumen (PYE) and plastomer bitumen (PYP). Data are representative for a PYE top layer bitumen waterproofing membrane used on the Swedish market. In the Nordic countries is bitumen waterproofing almost exclusively uses bitumen modified with SBS (styrene-butadiene-styrene).
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Bitumen-based waterproofing layers are mainly used on roofs and are normally laid in several layers, but there are also alternatives with one layer, but then requires a roof with a roof slope of at least 1:2 - 1:20.
Resources.GeneralComment: The generic values are based on the market situation in Finland that is assumed to be representative for all Nordic countries and information gathered from the largest manufacturers products for bitumen roofing. The data for GWP A1-A3 are based on data gathered from said manufacturers and represent the common products. These manufacturers represent over 95 % of the Finnish bitumen roofing market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The manufacturing is done by heating the raw materials (bitumen and copolymers) to a specific temperature and mixing them. After this the mix is applied to the reinforcing structure (polyester or glass fibre). The resulting sheet is cooled and then faced with mineral granules. The bitumen is generally delivered hot from the petroleum refinery to the manufacturing site, where it’s heated further. Significant differences arise mainly from the amounts of bitumen and the SBS used in the products. As SBS has a large share of emission, using alternative copolymers to modify the bitumen would also change the GWP-GHG A1-A3 value.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the manufacturers of bitumen waterproofing layers and the products consumed on the Swedish market. The data on environmental impact are based on LCA calculations and have been compared with cross-sectoral EPDs for all European producers, where these values ​​for GWP are slightly higher.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: For modern bitumen-based waterproofing systems, a service life of up to 40 years can be assumed today.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When bitumen-based waterproofing systems are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by domestic production, but some imports do occur.

Resources.Name: Structural steel, all sorts, 80 % primary material

Names.EN: Structural steel, all sorts, 80 % primary material

Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Several relevant EPDs are available for steel products, and data is used for the most common variants, such as untreated and painted steel. Many of the EPDs are company-specific, but they are also generally useful since they represent several types of products. When the difference in environmental impact varies too much due to the type of metal blend used for the product type, the reported data is divided. However, if an average use of primary and secondary metals can be defined, only a single dataset is provided. Note that project-specific adaptations of the steel are normally made and must be reported separately. The construction product is reported excluding project-specific adaptations.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Structural steel refers to steel used in load-bearing structures in the construction industry, such as beams and columns.
Resources.GeneralComment: Recycled steel saves 60 to 90% of energy compared to primary steel production. The maximum share of scrap in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) is limited to about 20%. In electric arc furnace (EAF), the share can be up to 100%. However, today the recycled content in steel production is limited due to the limited availability of scrap metal. According to EN 15804, only “post-consumer recycling” is considered to have no upstream environmental impact from steel production. If the term scrap is used, it may also include process waste, which according to EN 15804 should be assigned the environmental impact from the upstream processes it has undergone. The current EPDs on the market do not take this into account, which is why steel generally based on “scrap” underestimates the environmental impact if the actual amount of post-consumer recycling is not reported in the EPD. This issue is not addressed in the current database and must be covered in future updates. The environmental data used here in the database are based on EPDs from various suppliers available on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Steel is produced based on technical specifications that are normally possible to achieve with primary as well as secondary resources.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the manufacturers of the steel products consumed on the Swedish market. The data on environmental impact are based on EPDs and have been compared with cross-sectoral EPDs for all European producers.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal to the construction of which it is a part of. Steel used in an exposed environment must normally be maintained.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When steel products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The market includes domestic manufacturers as well as imports and there are no statistics available on how much of the metal is consumed and its origin in the construction industry.

Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Steel sheets for cladding of walls and roofs including profiled sheets.
Resources.GeneralComment: Recycled steel saves 60 to 90% of energy compared to primary steel production. The maximum share of scrap in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) is limited to about 20%. In electric arc furnace (EAF), the share can be up to 100 %. However, today the recycled content in steel production is limited due to the limited availability of scrap metal. According to EN 15804, only “post-consumer recycling” is considered to have no upstream environmental impact from steel production. If the term scrap is used, it may also include process waste, which according to EN 15804 should be assigned the environmental impact from the upstream processes it has undergone. The current EPDs on the market do not take this into account, which is why steel generally based on “scrap” underestimates the environmental impact if the actual amount of post-consumer recycling is not reported in the EPD. This issue is not addressed in the current database and must be covered in future updates. The environmental data used here in the database are based on EPDs from various suppliers available on the Swedish market.

Resources.Name: Aluminium profile, primary
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Several relevant EPDs are available for aluminium products. Many of the EPDs are corporate/company specific values but also generally applicable because those represent several product types. Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Aluminium profiles including tubes and rods used in the construction industry. Aluminium is used in construction for example for the manufacture of doors, windows, facade panels, light ceilings, railings, fences, telecommunication masts, solar energy technology, HVAC devices, racks, ladders, and stairs. Aluminium profiles also provide frames to support large glazed surfaces such as verandas and curtain walls.
Resources.GeneralComment: Primary aluminium in the building product comes from 100% virgin aluminium ie 0% recycled. The most essential issues that affect the climate impact of aluminium products are the scrap content, the energy efficiency of the manufacturing process and the GHGs of the energy sources used. Compared to the production of primary aluminium, secondary aluminium ingot requires roughly 5% of the original energy consumption . All aluminium products can be recycled after use. Aluminium losses in melting are low, roughly 3%. The thermal energy from natural gas used to melt aluminium scrap in many recycling facilities contributes to the consumption of about 52% of the total non-renewable energy consumption for secondary ingot production. Correspondingly, natural gas contributes to 48% of GWP-GHG A1-A3. The manufacturing of primary aluminium ingot includes bauxite mining, alumina refining, electrolysis (including anode production and smelting), and primary ingot casting. Environmental data used here are based on EPDs from various suppliers that occur on the Swedish market and compared to European cross sectoral LCA data.

Resources.Name: Copper sheet, 51 % scrap-based
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Several relevant EPDs are available for copper products. Many of the EPDs are corporate/company specific values but also generally applicable because those represent several product types. When the difference in environmental impact vary too much for a product type and metal mix used the reported data are divided, but when an average use of primary and secondary metals are possible to define a single data set is reported.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Copper sheets are commonly used for various purposes, including roof and wall cladding.
Resources.GeneralComment: The greatest influence of the environmental impacts comes from extraction of the raw materials used (ores, concentrates). Copper concentrations in naturally occurring ores are typically between 0.2 and 2.5 %. Geologically, copper is associated with other valuable and precious metals. Since their natural concentrations are much lower, the ore needs careful treatment to maximize recovery yields. Modern mining techniques require less energy than in the past, making the recovery of small amounts of metal more viable. The first stage of ore extraction and processing are the main contributors to GWP-GHG A1-A3. The metal produced from ores and concentrates is referred to as primary copper production. Metal can also be produced by recycling the scrap generated during the operations of the downstream value chain, as well as from end-of-life products.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Copper is produced based on technical specifications that are normally possible to achieve with primary as well as secondary resources.

Resources.ComparativeProperty: When copper products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The market is mainly based on imports and there are no statistics available on how much of the metal is consumed and its origin in the construction industry. The European copper institute has published the environmental profile of copper products. The assessment covers around 90% of the EU’s production of both copper metal and copper products thus providing a representative profile in the European market.

Resources.Name: Cross-laminated timber, u 12 %, coniferius
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is representative of CLT made of coniferius, which is a solid wood construction product consisting of several (typically 3, 5, 7, or 8) bonded single-layer panels, arranged at right angles to each other.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: CLT has many aplications and can be used in walls, floors or roofs. In construction systems such as walls, floors and roofs, CLT panels serve as load-bearing elements.
Resources.GeneralComment: The environmental impact is based on the largest producers and their EPD are representative for the CLT consumed on the Swedish market. The use of fossil energy in the manufacturing  determine to large extend the GWP-GHG A1-A3 result. The Swedish producers (and latest updated EPDs) nowadays use reduction diesel, which consist of at least 25% biobased diesel. The conifer wood used for this generic data is a mix based on 71% spruce and 29% conifer, resulting in a dry raw-density of 394 kg dry matter per m³. The amount of resin used is about 1% PUR.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: CLT has a moisture content of 12% and CLT production is mainly based on electricity and sawn timber.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the major producers and thereby the major consumption of CLT used in Sweden.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of wood indoors is normally equal to the construction of which it is a part of. Wood in exposed outdoor environment normally needs maintenance during these 50 years.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When the products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by national producers. Since no statistic is available concerning domestic use the environmental impact is based on a plain average of the EPDs from the manufacturers.

Resources.Name: Brick, second firing (increased color variations)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for bricks used on the Swedish market. These data are valid for bricks manufactured  with an additional firing, so-called second firing. Second firing means that the facades become very multifaceted in the color changes. At the same time, the double firing makes the brick material more frost-resistant.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Second firing bricks are manufacturerd with different colors and sizes from different producers.
Resources.GeneralComment: Bricks are manufactured of clay, sand, lime and sawdust. The bricks are burned in a tunnel furnace at a high temperature, roughly 1050°C. The primary energy use varies between 2.0 – 4 MJ/kg of non-renewable energy and 0.5 MJ/kg of electricity. The use of combustion of fossil fuels is the dominant contribution to the products GHG emissions. Environmental data are based on EPDs for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology between the manufacturers is equivalent, but the fuel varies where fossil gas and oil dominate. An additive in the clay of limestone flour gives yellow brick. Manganese is used for brown or tan-black brick. Bricks are fired in cassettes at 1050°C. The actual firing takes two days in a modern tunnel kiln. The whole process is monitored so that all roof tiles to achieve an even hardness and a frost-resistant roof tile.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the bricks that are consumed on the Swedish market. Environmental data is based on EPDs collected during 2020.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Bricks in buildings usually do not need any maintenance during their dimensioned service life. Bricks are suitable for reuse.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When bricks are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: All bricks used in Sweden are imported (the last brickyard was located in Haga, Enköping, and closed in 2020). The largest imports come from Denmark, followed by Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany.

Resources.Name: Cellulose fibre, batts, unused paper
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data is represenatative for cellulose fibre thermal insulation as batts where the fibres are made from post-consumer paper waste. Fire retardants are added to the insulation.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Cellulose fibre as such is used as thermal insulation and sometimes also used as sound insulation or a combined function. Cellulose fibre has an intended use in a protected environment.
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG (A1-A3) applies to bats and can vary between different manufacturers and is based on LCA and available EPD data.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
Cellulose fiber is produced by unused newsprint and mixed with additives for structure, fire and microbial resistance. 
The amount of fire protection agent is about 5%. The product is used for thermal insulation of walls, ceilings and attics in buildingsI minor variation of the density for the same lambda value exists between different manufacturers, but the values on density given here and lambda value is representative for the products used on the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that is currently consumed on the Swedish market
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the the construction it is part of.
Resources.ComparativeProperty:
In order to assess thermal insulation the lambda value need to be used in combination with the fact that different product alternatives have different densities. With other words, thermal insulation cannot be compared per kg but in use conditions. 

Material data applicable for the generic resource are as follows;
Blowing wool, attic, 27-40 kg/m³, lambda 0.040 W/(mK)
Blowing wool, flooring, 40-65 kg/m³ lambda 0.039 W/(mK)
Blowing wool, walls, 40-65 kg/m³ lambda 0.039 W/(mK)
Batts 36 kg/m³ lambda 0.036 W/(mK)
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The consumption in Sweden is dominated by domestic producers and some import.

Resources.Name: Reused construction product
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The information is representative of a reused product in its existing condition, including 40 km of transport to a cold storage. According to EN 15804, a reused product has no environmental impact from the first use of the product. If the product is upgraded to be used in its new design, the environmental impact of this must be added.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Reuse of a product that does not require an upgrade, or if required, is included in other parts of the bill of resources used in the assessment of the construction works.
Resources.GeneralComment: The GWP-GHG (A1-A3) is 0 kg CO₂e for a reused product.

Resources.Name: Insulating glass (IG), double glazing (4-16-4)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for a double glazing window.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Insulating glass prevents heat loss through glass doors and windows. Insulating glass consists of several components: flat glass, spacer material that creates the space between the glass panes and allows any gas to be filled in the space between the panes. All these parts are assembled into a single sealed unit that holds the entire cassette together and helps prevent changes, especially in the air (or gas) between the glass panes. These complete units are called insulating glass units or IGUs.
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for floatglass varies between 0.95 -1.2 kg CO₂e/kg depending on supplier. Then other parts are added in the window pane with about 24% of GWP-GHG (A1-A3). The LCA values ​​are based on the largest importers to Sweden, where about two thirds of imported insulating glass comes from Poland, which has been taken into account in the transport data.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The difference in the manufacturing process and the composition of the insulating glass is small between manufacturers. All insulating glass are manufactured according to European standards. The weight for flat glass is 2.5 kg/mm and m².
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of double glazing insulating glass used in the Swedish market. The information is valid until new data are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is basically infinite, but in practice it corresponds to the time the glazed building element remains before it is demolished, which in this case has been set to 50 years.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The generic insulating glass weighs 20 kg/m². Floatglass may be surface-treated and glazed windows filled with gas, but this does no affect the GWP-GHG (A1-A3) significantly.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden consists of imports, mainly from Europe.

Resources.Name: Laminated safety glass (LSG)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: The data are representative of an untreated laminated safety glass in the form of flat glass.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Floatglass are used as raw-material for window production and is normally not handled on the construction site. Laminated safety glass (LSG) consists of at least two glass panes lying one on top of the other, with one or several layers of a tear-resistant, viscoelastic film posi­tioned between the panes, which consist of polyvinyl butyral (PVB).
Resources.GeneralComment: GWP-GHG (A1-A3) for floatglass varies between -10/+20 % CO₂e/kg depending on supplier. The LCA values ​​are based on the largest importers to Sweden and their EPDs.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: There are only minor differences in the manufacturing process and composition of laminated safety glass between manufacturers. Resources.Name: Nails, fasteners and fittings, primary steel

Names.EN: Nails, fasteners and fittings, primary steel
Names.SV: Spikar, fästdon och beslag, primär stål

Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Several relevant EPDs are available for steel products and are used as proxy data for steel nails, fasteners and fittings. Many of the EPDs are corporate/company specific values but also generally applicable because those represent several product types. When the difference in environmental impact vary too much for a product type and metal mix used, the reported data are divided. However, if an average use of primary and secondary metals can be defined, only a single data set is provided.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Data refers to all type of nails and fittings made of steel. The steel can be hot-dip galvanized or electro-galvanized.
Resources.GeneralComment: Recycled steel saves 60 to 90% of energy compared to primary steel production. The maximum share of scrap in basic oxygen furnace (BOF) is limited to about 20%. In electric arc furnace (EAF), the share can be up to 100 %. However, today the recycled content in steel production is limited due to the limited availability of scrap metal. According to EN 15804, only “post-consumer recycling” is considered to have no upstream environmental impact from steel production. If the term scrap is used, it may also include process waste, which according to EN 15804 should be assigned the environmental impact from the upstream processes it has undergone. The current EPDs on the market do not take this into account, which is why steel generally based on “scrap” underestimates the environmental impact if the actual amount of post-consumer recycling is not reported in the EPD. This issue is not addressed in the current database and must be covered in future updates. The environmental data used here in the database are based on EPDs from various suppliers available on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Steel is produced based on technical specifications that are normally possible to achieve with primary as well as secondary resources.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the manufacturers of the steel products consumed on the Swedish market. The data on environmental impact are based on EPDs and have been compared with cross-sectoral EPDs for all European producers.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal to the construction of which it is a part of. Steel used in an exposed environment must normally be maintained.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When steel products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: The market includes domestic manufacturers as well as imports and there are no statistics available on how much of the metal is consumed and its origin in the construction industry.

Resources.Name: Planed timber, u 16 %, coniferous
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Planed timber can be used directly in all construction works or used as an input in other wood-based products.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Planed timber is used for structural purposes, as cladding and as a component in wood based products. The average moisture ratio of the declared products is 16%. On request, wood with different moisture content can be delivered.
Resources.GeneralComment: The values are based on minor group of producers in Sweden that covers 25% of the total planed wood produced. The planed wood product can be produced in manufacturing facilities with both sawmill and planing mill in the same location (combination plant) and in manufacturing facilities working solely with planing (Standalone planing mill). Standalone planing mill purchases all sawn timber from several sawmills localized at various transport distances. The results here is valid for an average plant. In order to give an overall generic figure it is assumed that 20% of the planned timber origin from combined plants.  Sawn dried timber is produced in Sweden mainly based on domestic logs. When import occur it affects the GWP-GHG (A1-A3) where the transport (A2) of used sawn timber may increase significantly. The planed timber GWP-GHG (A1-A3) varies and an average value is 33.5 kg CO₂e/m³ for the companies that are involved in the inventory. The same species mix as for sawn timber is assumed to be valid for planed timber as well.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The environmental impact is based on a sector EPD that covers 58% of the total planed timber in Sweden. Dried planed timber has an average density of 455 kg/m³ and a moisture content of 16%. Sawn planed timber of spruce has an average density of 470 kg/m³ and 440 kg/m³ for pine. The moisture content for the dried wood is about 12-18%. Biogenic carbon storage is 715kg CO₂/m³.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data are representative of the largest producers and thus the majority of the planed timber consumption in Sweden. These data represent the year 2020, i.e., after the diesel reduction mandate was implemented, which is why the reported GWP is lower than before.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life of wood indoors is normally equal to the construction of which it is a part of. Wood exposed to outdoors normally needs maintenance during these 50 years.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When the products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Consumption in Sweden is dominated by domestic producers, which is why the background data used from Swedish sawmills can be considered representative of this consumption.

Resources.Name: Cement, type CEM II/A-LL 42.5 R
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Cement is an input for concrete and is thus a semi-finished product. Ready-mix concrete is normally purchased and is not normally mixed at the construction site unless in small quantities.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Cement is used as binder in concrete. Cement is a hydraulic binder that consists of finely ground, non-metallic inorganic compounds. Cement is produced by grinding cement clinker and other main or minor constituents. When water is added to cement, a cement paste is formed, which sets and hardens. After hardening, it retains its strength and stability even under water.
Resources.GeneralComment: Cement is used for concrete that is made from rock, gravel and cement, where the main raw material is limestone. In climate-improved concrete, part of the cement is replaced with alternative binders. Environmental data for the cement binders used are based on EPDs for commonly used cement grades on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The declared product is a cement conforming with the composition of Portland Limestone Cement CEM II/ALL 42.5 R, in accordance with EN 197-1.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The information is representative of the type of cement used in the Swedish market. The information is valid until new ones are published.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: Cement that is used for concrete and exposed outdoor or other wet environment is designed in respect to durability according to Eurocodes. The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of.  Concrete for buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When concrete products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account. The compact density is 3040 kg/m³ and bulk density is 1250 kg/m³.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Environmental data for cement can be considered as representative of the most widely used type of cement on the Swedish market.

Resources.Name: Brick beam
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Data are representative for a brick beam used on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: A brick beam is a horizontal structural element that spans openings such as portals, doors, windows and fireplaces. A brick beam made of bricks is manufacturerd with different colors and sizes from different producers. As a standard, brick beams are manufactured from 4 stone brick beams and up to 27 stones. Up to and including 13 stones, beams are manufactured in single shifts, after which they are manufactured as double shifts. So for example a 14 stone beam has 28 reinforced bricks and so on.
Resources.GeneralComment: Beams consist of bricks, steel rebars and concrete. Bricks are manufactured of clay, sand, lime and sawdust. The bricks are burned in a tunnel furnace at a high temperature, roughly 1050°C. The primary energy use varies between 2.0 – 4 MJ/kg of nonrenewable energy and 0.5 MJ/kg of electricity. The use of combustion of fossil fuels is the dominant contribution to the products GHG emissions. Environmental data are based on EPDs for suppliers to the domestic Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The technology between the manufacturers is equivalent, but the fuel varies where fossil gas and oil dominate. An additive in the clay of limestone flour gives yellow brick. Manganese is used for brown or tan-black brick. Bricks are fired in cassettes at 1050°C. The actual firing takes two days in a modern tunnel kiln. The whole process is monitored so that all bricks achieve an even hardness and a frost-resistant brick.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of a brick beam that are consumed on the Swedish market. Environmental data is based on the producers EPDs collected during 2020.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Bricks in buildings usually do not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life. Bricks are suitable for reuse.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When bricks are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: All bricks used in Sweden are imported (the last brickyard was located at Haga, Enköping and was closed in 2020, and a very small production based on old technology is nowadays left at Horns Tegelbruk). The largest imports come from Denmark and then from, Finland, the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.

Resources.Name: Hempcrete blocks
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet:
Data is representative for hemp fibre thermal insulation block. Hempcrete blocks are made by mixing hemp shives with limes and cement. The current product has a weight ratio between hemp and lime of 1:1.67. The data is also useful for other combinations with a maximum of 10% higher proportion of lime or lower proportion of lime (but not higher as these data would in such cases underestimate the climate impact).
The climate data for this resource can be used for hemp-lime sprayed on site in a building structure that has a weight ratio of hemp to lime of 1:1.22 (45 and 44% by weight respectively) and is then a conservative choice of data.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Hemp fibre as such is used as thermal insulation and sometimes also used as sound insulation or a combined function. In this case, a masonry block has been made from hemp and lime. Hemp fibre has an intended use in a protected environment. It is not needed to add fire retardants in hempcrete blocks.

Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The generic hempcrete block is a mixture of 31% Hemp shives and 63 % binder, where the binder used in the block's is mixture made of 80% dolomite lime (hydrated lime) and 20% cement. There is a variation of the density 310-350 kg/m³ for the same lambda value. The density given here and the lambda value are exemplary values of what is used on the market.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data is representative for the manufacturing process and products that is currently is consumed on the Swedish market.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: The service life is normally equal with the the construction it is part of.

Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: High-density fibreboard can be used both for building purposes (wall, roof, floor, air gaps) and for furniture and furnishings as well.
Resources.GeneralComment:
High-density fibreboard (HDF) represents a wooden product based on wood fibres manufactured in a dry process. Apart from wood fibres, HDF also comprises binding agents (about 14%) and other additives.
GWP (A1-A3) for wood-based panels can vary greatly between different manufacturers. To achieve a common result, the biogenic carbon stored in products is subtracted, so that the climate impact is reported as GWP-GHG. Even after this, there can be significant differences between manufacturers which, without access to the underlying LCA report, are difficult to explain. One difference may be the environmental impact allocated to the wood raw material.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The data applies to HDF made of softwood and a density of about 850 kg/m3. The density may vary between different manufacturers.

The environmental data for the cements used are based on EPDs for commonly used types of cement on the Swedish market.

However, it is likely that the strength class will at least be C32/40, and that maximal gravel diameter is 8 mm and a water cement/binder ratio of at least 0.55.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are based on a Swedish producers of ready-mixed concrete and the concrete recipes they use and a class that is representative for the mortar/concrete filler used. Resources.Name: Rapid drying concrete, exposure class XC1

Names.EN: Rapid drying concrete, exposure class XC1

Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet:
The concrete product is common in housing construction in parts where the drying time is decisive. So-called drying concrete has properties adapted to fast and reliable drying time and is used indoors in buildings for walls and joists. Dry concrete is not an unambiguous concrete quality but has varying properties such as vct/vbt, strength class, exposure class etc. The resource refers to a generic drying concrete for indoor purposes. If more properties are required for a concrete, information from a supplier must be used. Normally, concrete is reinforced. Reinforcement is handled as a separate resource in this database.
For testing compressive strength, EN 206 refers to the following standard: EN 12390-3, Testing hardened concrete — Part 3: Compressive strength of test specimens. In Table 12 of EN 206 specifies "Compressive strength classes for normal concrete and heavy concrete". This is supplemented in SS 137003 with "Table 1 — Intermediate classes for compressive strength".
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Concrete for houses is used especially for load-bearing parts of the structure. The concrete composition is controlled, in addition to compressive strength of exposure class, but also of other properties e.g. consistence, time for curing and drying.
Resources.GeneralComment: Concrete is made from rock, gravel and cement where the main raw material is limestone. I climate-improved concrete is part of the cement replaced with alternative binders. The data given, based on compressive strength class, represent commonly used concrete recipes on the market. Factory data for module A3 is based on data from a large number of EPDs. Of the reported value for climate impact, the contribution from the manufacturing process (A3) is relatively small in relation to the contribution from the cement, which normally accounts for more than 90 % of the concrete's climate impact in module A1-A3. Environmental data for the cement binders used are based on EPDs for commonly used cement grades on the Swedish market.
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The compressive strength class of the concrete follows the standard EN 206:2013+A1:2016 and SS 137003:2015.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: The data given are representative of the Swedish producers of ready-mixed concrete and the concrete recipes they use. These data have been produced during the year 2020. The data given on environmental impact is based on current EPDs for cement, additives and factory data.
Resources.RefServiceLifeNormalComment: Concrete exposed to outdoors or other wet environment is designed in respect to durability according to Eurocodes. The service life is normally equal with the construction it is part of. Concrete for buildings usually does not need any maintenance during its dimensioned service life.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: When concrete products are compared with other materials or material combinations, the assessment must be made in the intended use and in a life cycle perspective, ie the entire life cycle must be taken into account.
Resources.AnnualSupplyOrProductionVolume: Concrete manufacturers are spread all over the country and environmental data can be considered representative when the used recipes and binder mixes reflect the production of all these manufacturers, as well as being based on several EPDs.

Resources.Name: Diesel MK3, reduction obligation (2024)
Resources.UseAdviceForDataSet: Environmental data is representative of the diesel purchased in Sweden. Diesel's climate performance is governed by the reduction obligation and increased amount of biofuels, which is determined by the government. The Swedish Energy Agency has produced a new regulation, STEMFS 2025:​3, on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions through the incorporation of biofuels in petrol and diesel fuels.
Resources.TechnologicalApplicability: Diesel is purchased and burned in various machines and vehicles, i.e. a WtW (Well to Wheel) scope.
Resources.GeneralComment: The climate impact from Diesel MK3 was 90,2 g CO₂e/MJ, the share of renewable energy was 6,2 percent in 2024 (Energimyndigheten Drivmedel 2024).
Resources.TechnologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: The calculation of greenhouse gas emissions according to the reduction obligation was based on the standard values ​​for the fossil fuels established in an additional directive to the fuel quality directive 2015/652/EU and a mixture of renewables.
Resources.TimeRepresentativenessDescription: Data is representative for the year 2024.
Resources.ComparativeProperty: The calculation method follows "Renewable Energy Directive" (RED) 2018/2001/EU and the “FQD Implementing Directive” EU 2015/652. However, there is a difference between these directives compared to core product calculations rules for construction products (EN 15804). The major difference is that EN 15804 use an economical allocation approach for pre-consumer waste/recycling, why fuels based on this kind of raw materials would result in a higher value if EN 15804 was to be followed. This difference is not relevant for the LCA figures given here, but may arise if these data are replaced with specific LCA data from a manufacturer that complies with the EC directives.
